name: agent-soupsieve-paths-20261113

findings.affected_feature: CMS encryption to attacker-controlled EC recipient
findings.basis: No ELF imports CMS_encrypt/CMS_encrypt_ex, no current Python call site performs CMS envelope encryption, and no openssl CLI exists in the Agent. The installed separate cryptography PKCS7 wrapper also rejects EC recipients before encryption; the recorded synthetic EC-certificate test exercises that real boundary.

The only consumer of the Debian libssl is CPython _ssl, which selects TLS method objects, imports no QUIC methods and performs no dynamic lookup. The reviewed HTTP stack exposes no HTTP/3 or QUIC call site; ordinary TLS negotiation cannot select the separate QUIC transport.

No current application or dependency call site requests AES-GCM-SIV. The system-library path is conventional TLS plus hashing; its actual TLS cipher set contains no GCM-SIV. The separate cryptography implementation is explicitly identified rather than conflated with Debian libcrypto; its installed API definitions are not application call sites.
The same exact TLS-method and caller closure excludes the QUIC CRYPTO-stream processing entry path. This does not claim that a general-purpose QUIC client is unaffected.

The exact current system-library consumers do not select AES-GCM-SIV. Separately, the installed high-level cryptography wrapper rejects tested IV lengths 0,11,13,16 and accepts 12; it has no incremental-update API. These observations are not an upstream fixed-binary claim.
The exact245 extra conversion-module ELF payloads contain neither affected libc implementation nor its entry points. The real libc.so.6 belongs to libc6 and is reviewed separately.

The exact current client-only application does not select POSIX/GNU regex, libc regex wrappers or Kerberos local authorization. The sole regcomp/regexec/regfree consumer is Kerberos local mapping; actual libpq GSS client APIs do not invoke its separate localname callbacks. BSD cleanup is conditional on a re_comp-initialized shared buffer and no current entry initializes it.

The exact current native/Python bindings and libc internal-wrapper review select no affected wide scanf entry. The only non-libc target-name occurrences are independently verified nonallocated greenlet debug strings; application FFI is fixed unrelated binding, not user-selected native dispatch.
